title: Review repair A: attempt git identity, integrate on the collected head, dispose rejected attempts, adopt by tick id
description:
BLOCKERS from the final review (spec + correctness reviewers, both independently): (1) internal/reconcile/integrate.go:121 durableAttemptHead merges origin's tick/<id> head whenever it exists and never compares it with the collected, boundary-checked local head (collect.go:63 HeadSHA); a failed final push (supervisor.go:197-208 ignores push_failed) or a report written before the last push makes the reconciler merge a stale subset, close the tick, then cleanUp disposes with a Reason which skips dispose.go:64's onRemote safety and deletes the unpushed commits — false completion plus lost write. (2) dispatch.go:409 gives every attempt of every run of a tick the same write_ref refs/heads/tick/<id>, so a second attempt/run is refused RefusedLive by makeWorktree (executor.go:416-420, branch exists) and pushes collide non-fast-forward silently (git.go:250-253); RESULT-cc5.md shows the operator deleting tick branches by hand as the workaround. (3) Nothing disposes a rejected attempt (Dispose only from cleanUp after close, dispatch.go:668) so its worktree and branch survive forever and a same-checkout redispatch is impossible. Fix in internal/reconcile (and the minimal executor seam if unavoidable — coordinate through the JobSpec, do not rewrite internal/exec/subprocess; the sibling repair B owns that package): (a) write_ref carries run+attempt identity per the SPEC §4.3 golden shape refs/heads/ticfac/run-<run>/tick-<id>/attempt-<n> (check contracts/job-protocol.json's golden and credential write_ref_prefix rules and keep both readers happy); (b) integrate refuses — or pushes local first, refusing on non-fast-forward — whenever the collected HeadSHA differs from origin's head, and never merges a head that was not collected; (c) a rejected attempt is cancelled and disposed (worktree + local branch) by the reconciler, but a branch whose head is not on the remote is NEVER deleted (dispose safety must not be skippable by Reason); (d) dispatch.go:262 ConflictExists path verifies recorded.TickID == tick before adopting, re-fetching and recomputing the number on mismatch, and sets the attempt on the checkpoint; (e) adopt() replays the tracker Claim when the tick is still unclaimed (crash between marker and claim, dispatch.go:289); (f) the boundary check's base comes from the reconciler's durable marker (marker.BaseSHA), not only from attempt.json the worker's uid can rewrite (collect.go:59-70 — compare and refuse on mismatch); (g) mergeInWorktree's message carries the real attempt number (integrate.go ~1006). Tests: a fixture where the supervisor's final push fails (local ahead of remote) must NOT close the tick and must NOT lose the commits; same-checkout restart after a rejected attempt dispatches attempt n+1 on a fresh ref; ConflictExists with a foreign tick's marker is not adopted; the three restart tests and the lifecycle suite stay green. Use -timeout 45m when running the reconcile package.

## How this fits
Wave 8 of epic qeu (final-review repairs), three tickets in parallel. You own: internal/reconcile (code) — sibling B owns internal/exec/subprocess and the doc lines it names; sibling C owns .github/, scripts/, internal/runstate, gate.go output-capture lines and restart_test.go. The reviewer reports are at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-peterengelbrecht-Development-ticfac/1687f85b-9680-4c8b-ad98-ebe61eb3bfb3/scratchpad/review/findings-all.md (read-only, on this host). Integration commit 06a82eb57da464ebcea04d910fac4bfd02c227f9 on epic/qeu. The reconcile package takes ~10 minutes: run it with go test -short -timeout 45m and never in the background. Verify your base: git merge-base --is-ancestor 06a82eb57da464ebcea04d910fac4bfd02c227f9 HEAD.
